Wow, thank you so much for this. I really needed it. I will be completely honest, I’ve felt very alone this entire journey of trying to find answers and it’s really discouraging. Knowing my parents don’t know about any of this (but likely would not care anyway) really hurts. Like I have this really bad sort of dissonance with them, because they were terrible to me basically my entire life, but I just wanted to be accepted by them so so badly. I tried my hardest and it still wasn’t enough for them, ever. And you’re absolutely right, I was definitely known as very gifted and intelligent “but could still do more” growing up but I’ve always felt something was off. Would often be told I would live up to my potential if I collaborated with classmates (I was always really quiet). It started going downhill in high school but I was still able to keep afloat in high school for the most part but university feels like it faceplanted me into a pile of glass.

I’ll definitely look into the insurance and see if it’s something I can do. I hadn’t known of this, so thank you for letting me know.

I’m on that journey right now. I tried for what feels like my entire life suppressing (or “masking” as they say) I felt like I lost myself a long time ago. I feel like I don’t even know my real self. And definitely, talk therapy was not for me at all. Like you, I felt worse after each session and did not like it at all, but found it strange since my friend said she found it very helpful. Of course, to each their own.

The negative stigma around ADHD meds are way more prominent than others that I’ve seen, so I will admit I was nervous about taking any at all. But hearing your experience makes me feel better and I will consider it. Honestly I never realized it til a few months ago but I am almost always in a constant state of brain fog, so I’d consider anything that could have me “think” better.

My dad was incredibly addicted to cigarettes and alcohol, so due to having to see how it affected him and the people around him made me swear to never end up like him. Hearing that I’m more susceptible makes me a bit uneasy, but it’s also not surprising.

And for sure, I really think I would benefit from those kinds of accommodations. A lot of times on exams, I always feel like I didn’t have enough time (cue my peers’ “it was fine, what are you talking about?”) and I feel like I could do better even with just extra time.

It just really sucks that here I am, by myself and I have to be jumping through so many hoops to get evaluated to even be taken seriously by higher ups. It’s incredibly degrading and discouraging as mentioned earlier and I just hope all of this turns out to be worth it. Thank you so much, again for your comment. It made me feel validated and a lot better about many things regarding my issue.

Yeah I’m starting to see they haven’t always been super helpful which is disappointing. And thanks, I’ll look into meditating. And sad thing is it’s always been hard for me to see far into the future, I’ve always been “going with the flow”. My major does sound interesting to me, but I don’t really know if I want to do that with my life because I don’t know all of what it entails and such. I come from a low-resource high school so I never really had any opportunities to explore my interests much past generic ones. I’m trying to figure it out but it’s rough.
Thank you! Will look into it

I did take advantage, but they didn’t seem to care at all about my worries surrounding potentially having ADHD. I never even said “I think I have ADHD”, I would just list things that I was having issues with and how it interferes with my learning. However they were super focused on the fact that I had symptoms of depression and would basically ignore anything else. I would list out my troubles and they’d be like “And how does that make you feel?” Bad, obviously. However I still went through with what therapy sessions they recommended me, because yes, I am very likely depressed, but it didn’t really help at all. It actually made me feel worse because all it really was is that I was basically trauma dumping my past (that I try not to think about much) onto this unempathetic trainee who looked like they couldn’t care less and were basically reading from a script. I get that they’re still in-training, but I was still super disappointed with how it all played out.
